title: PDF Has Transparency or Layers: How to Flatten It for Print (IngramSpark & KDP) | SparkPrep
h1: How to fix "PDF contains transparency or layers"
description: Your print PDF has live transparency or layers, so it was rejected or may print wrong. What that means and how to flatten it for IngramSpark and KDP.
platforms: IngramSpark · Amazon KDP · Barnes & Noble Press · Lulu
lead: Shadows, see-through effects and layers look fine on screen. In print, they can turn into white boxes or missing art.
error: The PDF contains live transparency or layers that must be flattened
errorNote: Paraphrased. Each printer words this a little differently.
why:
Drop shadows, glows, faded images and see-through shapes are all transparency. Design programs also keep your art in layers. Printing systems can handle these unevenly, so a shadow can print as a box or a layer can go missing.

The PDF/X-1a print standard, which IngramSpark asks for, doesn't allow live transparency, so everything must be flattened into one finished image. KDP recommends flattening too.
manual: Open your original file (InDesign, Illustrator, Photoshop or Canva).
Flatten it: in Photoshop use Layer → Flatten Image; in InDesign or Illustrator use Object → Flatten Transparency (High Resolution).
Check shadows, glows and faded areas still look right after flattening.
Re-export as PDF/X-1a:2001, which also removes layers.
Re-upload it to your printer and wait for the file review again. If it fails, you start over.

cta.text: SparkPrep spots live transparency and layers on every page, flattens them for you, and exports a PDF/X-1a your printer accepts.

faq.q: What does flattening a PDF mean?
faq.a: It merges all layers and see-through effects into one finished image per page, so it prints exactly as it looks.
When you download as PDF Print, tick the "Flatten PDF" box. Then check the PDF before uploading, especially pages with shadows or faded images.
